correctness.rationale: The environment generator has an explicit refresh spectral gap µ on mean-zero L²; bounded analytic jump perturbations justify a stationary-density and Poisson-corrector expansion at every fixed µ>0. The adjoint first-order density and field derivative are calculated independently; the carré-du-champ includes both walker and refreshing jumps. The first-chaos Fourier multipliers produce two explicit integrals, and periodic integration by parts proves the universal difference exactly. The sign is positive with a fixed-µ O(ε⁴) remainder for sufficiently small nonzero ε. Finite-ring Markov generator and high-accuracy quadrature checks passed; these checks were not used in place of infinite-lattice proof. Main risks: proper bias normalization and no uniformity as µ→0 are explicitly scoped.

value.rationale: The weak-disorder coefficient is a natural, dimensionless response observable in a new dynamical conductance model. It supplies the exact universal magnitude and sign at EVERY positive refresh rate, sharpening an existential Einstein-relation counterexample; it also identifies a noncommutative fast-refresh paradox, where even infinitely rapid independent refreshing leaves an O(ε²) normalized-rate mobility defect. The coefficient responds to a genuine model question, not a reparameterized textbook exercise. Fixed-µ scope prevents unsupported global-strength claims.
